  • Method Details

    • applySlimyEye

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult applySlimyEye(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity target)
      The Slimy Eye apply verb, server side: a target whose verdict is EyeItemService.Verdict.CAN_HAVE gains eyes carrying the stack's appearance on a freshly rolled placement variant, consuming one eye. Any other target refuses (FAIL) and consumes nothing, as does another player mayAffect(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity) protects. Both the mob path (interact(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity)) and the sneak self-apply (SlimyEyeItem#use) route through here. Vanilla records no item use for either, so this does.

    • applySlimyEye

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult applySlimyEye(net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack, net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity skull, net.minecraft.core.Direction face)
      The Slimy Eye apply verb for a placed mob head, server side, clicked on its face: a head whose verdict is EyeItemService.Verdict.CAN_HAVE gains eyes carrying the stack's appearance on a freshly rolled placement variant, consuming one eye outside creative. The player must be allowed to use the item on that block, as placing a block there would require. Otherwise it refuses (FAIL) and consumes nothing.

    • harvestSkull

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult harvestSkull(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer player, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity skull, net.minecraft.core.Direction face)
      The Optometrist harvest for a placed mob head, server side, clicked on its face: one Googly Eye carrying the head's effective appearance pops out of the block, the head loses its eyes, the shears in hand lose one durability, the shearing sound plays, and GameEvent.SHEAR is emitted. The player must be allowed to use the shears on that block. Returns InteractionResult.PASS when it doesn't apply (no eyes, not allowed, googlyEyesEnabled off).

    • interact

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult interact(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.entity.Entity target)
      Route supported entities through normal loader interaction hooks. Eligible application and harvesting are predicted on the client, so success also consumes the target's own use, and on Fabric the click's second interact packet: that packet's callback would otherwise find a just-harvested mob eyeless and let vanilla shear it. Irrelevant actions pass through to vanilla. Spectators pass here and at the other use entry points because the loaders' use hooks can fire before vanilla's spectator test.

    • markHeadDrop

      public static void markHeadDrop(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack stack)
      Give a head item an eyed mob drops in its death loot the mob's whole eye state, when the head is the mob's own kind (SkullEyeState.entityFor(net.minecraft.world.level.block.Block)) and carries no eyes yet, so the placed head shows the mob's arrangement and colors. Players are left out: their death drops are their inventory. Each loader routes every stack of the death-loot phase here; any other stack is left alone.

    • onDeath

      public static void onDeath(net.minecraft.world.entity.LivingEntity mob, net.minecraft.world.damagesource.DamageSource source, Consumer<net.minecraft.world.item.ItemStack> dropSink)
      Attempt the shears-on-kill harvest, routing the resulting eye through each loader's death-loot phase: Forge adds it to the LivingDropsEvent collection, Fabric spawns it from a dropAllDeathLoot mixin at the same point. Neither depends on doMobLoot, so the rule is checked here.

    • selfRemoveWithShears

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult selfRemoveWithShears(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand)
      Sneak + right-click air with shears to shear your own eyes off — the self-serve counterpart to another player having applied a Slimy Eye to you. One Googly Eye drops carrying your effective appearance and the shears lose one durability. Optometrist shears do it cleanly; plain shears additionally deal one melee hit's worth of ModContent.SELF_SHEAR damage, which has no attacker so PvP and team rules don't cancel it. Returns InteractionResult.PASS when it doesn't apply (spectating, not sneaking, not shears, no eyes, googlyEyesEnabled off) so the vanilla item use proceeds.

    • useOnSkull

      public static net.minecraft.world.InteractionResult useOnSkull(net.minecraft.world.entity.player.Player player, net.minecraft.world.level.Level level, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand hand, net.minecraft.world.phys.BlockHitResult hit)
      Right-click-on-block entry point for both eye items aimed at a placed mob head: a Slimy Eye goes to applySlimyEye(ItemStack, ServerPlayer, BlockEntity, Direction), Optometrist shears on an eyed head to harvestSkull(net.minecraft.server.level.ServerPlayer, net.minecraft.world.InteractionHand, net.minecraft.world.level.block.entity.BlockEntity, net.minecraft.core.Direction). The client answers InteractionResult.SUCCESS in exactly those cases, so it neither runs nor sends the item's own use on top (a sneaking player's self-apply or self-shear). Anything else, including plain shears or a spectator's click, returns InteractionResult.PASS. The Slimy Eye comes here rather than through Item#useOn for the reason a mob's click does: a head block can have a use of its own that takes the click first, as Twilight Forest's trophies do.
